We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $u\cdot (\frac{1}{2}u),$ we multiply $u\cdot u$ by $\frac{1}{2}.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (\frac{1}{2}u) & =\frac{1}{2}(u\cdot u) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 15 \\  & =\frac{15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (\frac{3}{4}v),$ we compute $u\cdot v$ first and then multiply the result by $\frac{3}{4}.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (\frac{3}{4}v) & =\frac{3}{4}(u\cdot v) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}((-1)\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 2) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(3+3+4+2) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 12 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{u\cdot (\frac{1}{2}u)}{u\cdot (\frac{3}{4}v)} & =\frac{(\frac{15}{2})}{9}=\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
